description: A Java routine's RETURNS clause may carry TYPE PARAMETERS - VARCHAR(100), DECIMAL(10,2), NUMBER(5), TIMESTAMP(9), TIMESTAMP_NTZ(6), and for procedures VARCHAR(50) and DECIMAL(15,4) - and the routine still creates and answers. The parameters are part of the signature's shape but not of its identity: two overloads may declare different return widths, and CREATE OR REPLACE may widen the return type of an existing routine, after which the new handler's longer value comes back whole. Declaring no parameters at all keeps working, which is the backward-compatible case. Converted 1:1 from udf/ReturnTypeParametersTest (now retired), a JDBC test whose statements are all plain SQL. Five tests carried Assumptions.assumeFalse(isLiveSnowflake()) and become skip snowflake with those reasons kept: Snowflake validates a Java handler's signature against the declared SQL type far more strictly - NUMBER and DECIMAL will not accept a double handler and TIMESTAMP will not accept a String one - and a Java stored procedure there must take a Session as its first handler argument.
